Chapter 7: Creating Social Support—Harnessing the Power of Community.
You know, changing habits or making big shifts in your life can feel overwhelming if you’re trying to do it all on your own. But here’s the thing: we’re wired to be social, and the people around us have a huge impact on what feels possible.
When your friends, coworkers, or family support you—or even just expect you to act a certain way—suddenly, change doesn’t seem so hard. It starts to feel normal, even exciting.
Social support shows up in all sorts of ways. Sometimes, it’s official—like having a peer group or a buddy to check in with. Other times, it’s just seeing people you respect take on the same challenge.
At work, you might notice “champions”—those folks who really live out the new behaviors. They’re the ones others look to for guidance and inspiration. And in your personal life? Just telling your goals to a friend or family member can make you feel more committed and connected.
So, how can you build this kind of support around you? Here are a few ideas to get started.
First, look for or create a community where the change you want is already happening. Maybe it’s a club, an online group, or just a circle of people who “get it.”
Next, find allies—those people who will cheer you on, set an example, or help keep you on track. Having someone in your corner makes a world of difference.
And don’t forget to make your progress visible. Share your wins and milestones—even the little ones. It not only boosts your own motivation, but it inspires others, too.
Think about a company rolling out new software. They might pick “super-users”—people who help others learn the ropes and celebrate every success. Or picture someone trying to quit smoking. Maybe they join a support group, or simply let close friends know about their goal so they can offer encouragement when it’s needed most.
There’s something called social proof—a fancy way of saying we look to others to figure out what’s normal. When you see a group embracing change, it suddenly feels like the natural thing to do.
And that group momentum? It keeps the change going, long after the initial excitement has worn off.
So if you’re looking to make a change stick, remember: don’t go it alone. Lean on your community, and let their support make the journey lighter.
